core_obligations: Decompose R into a product of rings R_{ij} so that M' and M'' have constant rank i and j over each factor, reducing the general case to the constant rank case (proof lines 36296-36301).
Reduce in that case to constructing a canonical map of exterior powers wedge^i(M') tensor wedge^j(M'') -> wedge^{i+j}(M) (proof lines 36301-36305).

Choose bases-like data: elements m'_1, ..., m'_i of M', their images m_1, ..., m_i in M, elements m''_1, ..., m''_j of M'', and chosen lifts m_{i+1}, ..., m_{i+j} in M, and state the intended rule (proof lines 36306-36316).
Establish that the displayed rule is well defined and an isomorphism; the author states that this detailed verification is omitted (proof line 36317).
difficulty_reason: The statement asks for a canonical isomorphism det(M') tensor det(M'') -> det(M) attached to a short exact sequence of finite projective R-modules (source lines 36282-36293). The difficulty is not in finding a map but in making it canonical: the proof first decomposes R into a product of rings indexed by the rank pairs (i, j) of the two outer modules, so that the ranks become constant (proof lines 36296-36301), and then has to produce a map between exterior powers that does not depend on the choices made. The construction uses chosen elements m'_1, ..., m'_i of M' and lifts m_{i+1}, ..., m_{i+j} of chosen elements of M'' (proof lines 36306-36316); the well-definedness and bijectivity of that rule is exactly the part the author states is omitted, and it is the substantive content of the lemma.
